prompts.question: Consider the functions (f(x)=2^x) and (g(x)=5(1/2)^x). What information tells you whether the functions are increasing or decreasing?
prompts.answer: the value of (b); If (b>1), the function is increasing and if (b<1), the function is decreasing.

prompts.question: How do the asymptote and the (y)-intercept of (g(x)) compare to the asymptote and the (y)-intercept of (f(x))?
prompts.answer: The asymptote is the same for both functions, the (x)-axis. The (y)-intercept of (f(x)) is 1. The (y)-intercept of (g(x)) is 0.
notes: Printed teacher answer says both asymptotes are the (x)-axis; likely (g) has asymptote (y=1), as stated in the worked solution. Additional Examples are available at SavvasRealize.com. Digital controls: Go back, ESSENTIAL QUESTION, SOLUTION.

context.text: Additional Examples. ADDITIONAL EXAMPLE 2 Graph the function (g(x)=-4^x+1). Describe the graph in terms of transformations of the parent function (f(x)=4^x). Since the sign of (a) changed, the function is reflected across the (x)-axis. By adding a constant (k=1), the function shifts vertically by 1 unit. The (y)-intercept changes from 1 to (-1) due to the reflection, then is translated vertically 1 unit to ((0,0)) due to the value of (k). The horizontal asymptote changes from (y=0) to (y=1). Example 2 Help students transition to graphing transformations of exponential functions with this additional example.

prompts.question: What misconception should I watch for?
prompts.answer: You may confuse reflection across the axes. Recall that if the (y)-value is multiplied by (-1), as in this case, with (g(x)=-3^x), the reflection is across the (x)-axis. Each (y)-value is replaced by its opposite.

prompts.question: How can you tell by the description of the value of the printer whether (0<b<1) or (b>1)?
prompts.answer: (0<b<1) because the value of the printer is decreasing.

context.text: Elicit and Use Evidence of Student Thinking

prompts.question: Does your answer make sense? Explain.
prompts.answer: Sample: The original value of the printer was $35,750 and the value decreases at a rate of 22% per year. That is a decrease of $7,865 the first year. If the value decreased at a constant rate, it would be less than $13,000 after three years. But each year, the value of the printer is less than it was the previous year. This means that 22% of the value is less in any given year than it was the previous year. So each year, the value decreases by a smaller amount than it did the previous year, making $16,965 a reasonable answer.

prompts.question: What part of an exponential function (f(x)=a· b^x) determines how rapidly the function will grow?
prompts.answer: The value of (b) determines how rapidly an exponential function grows. For (b>1), the larger (b) is, the more rapidly the function will grow.

prompts.question: Describe (b) in terms of a ratio.
prompts.answer: The growth or decay factor of an exponential function is the ratio of successive (y)-coordinates. So, (b=(f(1))/(f(0))) or (b=(f(2))/(f(1))).
